topic_title: Describe the purpose and function of data analysis
cmp_edition: IFoA CS1 Core Reading / CMP · 2026 syllabus alignment

mission.display_title: Name why actuarial data analysis exists
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to give you a professional purpose map for data analysis (aims, stages, sources, and reproducibility) so every later EDA and modelling day answers a named aim rather than wandering in tables.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to distinguish descriptive, inferential, and predictive aims before opening deep CMP pages, and to name one reproducibility element they will protect. So Day 1 sets Study Sensei habits, not a syllabus skim.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'CS1 starts with data' to 'I can state the aim of an analysis, the stage I am in, the source limitations I inherit, and what makes the work reproducible.'
mission.learning_objective: Explain the aims of a data analysis and outline the stages and reproducibility elements needed to conduct one for a real-world actuarial problem.
mission.concept_focus: Aims (descriptive / inferential / predictive) → analysis stages → data sources → reproducibility.
mission.prior_bridge: Cold start on the CS1 first-pass spine. You are opening Campaign Alpha. There is no prior Campaign day. Bring only willingness to treat data analysis as professional work with an aim, not as plotting for its own sake.
mission.why_now: 1.1 is the lawful first Learning Mode node on the CS1 2026 spine; examiners and workplace briefs expect you to state the aim of an analysis before choosing tools; without this map, exploratory work in 1.2 becomes undirected chart-making.
mission.expected_benefit: A four-part purpose map you can defend closed-book. Study Progress for today's Session, not mastery of all data-analysis tooling.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Alpha Day 1 because the official spine begins at 1.1; the educational gap is purpose and function, not jumping into correlation formulae.
success_criteria: Closed-book, name the three primary aims of data analysis (descriptive, inferential, predictive) with one actuarial-flavoured example each.
List the main stages of a data analysis in order and say which stage you are in when exploring raw variables.
Name two characteristics of a data source that change how you trust results, and one element required for reproducibility.
task_descriptions: Sketch Aims / Stages / Sources / Reproducibility as four boxes before opening the CMP.
Complete Guided Reading through the CMP treatment of aims, stages, sources, and reproducibility for Syllabus 1.1.
Closed-book: deliver the purpose map against today's success criteria.

session.session_educational_purpose: This Session exists to execute today's Mission: build and stress-test a closed-book purpose map for data analysis using selective CMP reading and retrieval. Not to survey every tool in the subject.
session.session_tutor_purpose: In this hour I will set focus questions on aims, stages, sources, and reproducibility, exit while the candidate works the CMP alone, then force a closed-book purpose-map retrieval. So Day 1 success criteria are stress-tested, not merely claimed.
session.wrap_up: Session complete for Name why actuarial data analysis exists. You practised selective CMP reading on Syllabus 1.1 and stress-tested the aims → stages → sources → reproducibility map. This is Study Progress for today's block. Not Topic Complete for all of 1.1, and not mastery of EDA techniques (that begins tomorrow).
session.confidence_prompt: How confident are you that you could explain the three aims and one reproducibility element closed-book tomorrow morning? Rate 1–5 and give one honest warrant.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: aims of data analysis
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name the three primary aims of a data analysis used in CS1. For each aim, give one short actuarial-flavoured example (one sentence each).
knowledge_checks.body: CMP closed. Distinguish descriptive vs inferential vs predictive with concrete examples.
hints: Descriptive summarises what is in the data; inferential generalises to a population; predictive forecasts unseen outcomes.
Think claims, pricing, and reserving contexts for examples. Keep them short.
knowledge_checks.explanation: CS1 frames data analysis around descriptive, inferential, and predictive aims. Confusing summarising a sample with making a population claim is a classic first-week error.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Descriptive: summarise claim sizes in a portfolio year. Inferential: estimate mean claim severity for the population of similar risks. Predictive: forecast next year's claim count for pricing.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Listing tools (plots, means) instead of aims, or collapsing all three into 'look at data.'
success_criteria: Each aim has a distinct, plausible example.
Examples do not confuse aim with tool.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: stages, sources, reproducibility
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) List the main stages of a data analysis in a sensible order and mark which stage exploratory work sits in. (2) Name two source characteristics that change how you trust results. (3) Name one element required to keep an analysis reproducible.
knowledge_checks.body: Connect stages to sources and reproducibility. Not tool names alone.
hints: Stages typically run from problem framing through data acquisition, cleaning/EDA, modelling/inference, and communication.
Source cues: sampling frame, bias, granularity, volume/velocity for large sets.
Reproducibility: code, data version, documentation, seed, environment. Name at least one clearly.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Purpose and function includes knowing where you are in the pipeline, what the data can support, and how another analyst could repeat the work.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Stages: define aim → obtain data → clean/explore → analyse/infer or predict → communicate. EDA sits in explore/clean. Sources: biased sample; coarse granularity. Reproducibility: versioned data and scripted code path.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Saying 'be careful with data' without naming source traits or a concrete reproducibility element.
